decision_point: Initial VPR: who records the indicators
rule_summary_en: The officers instructing the case complete the VPR, never the victim, and only with sufficient, corroborated information from all available sources; no victim leaves the station without an assessment and level-based measures.
correction_note: Added the "never leaves without assessment and measures" duty (1.3).
accountability_trail: Indicators and result go to court in the automated report (2019-R16).
interpretive_note: Which indicators are marked is officer judgement (made explicit in Protocolo Cero 2.3, C21-IND).

rule_summary_en: The system assigns one of five levels automatically: no apreciado, bajo, medio, alto, extremo.
interpretive_note: Weights and cut-offs of VPR5.0 are not in the instruction (Module 2 covers only VPR4.0, 2016).

decision_point: Officer adjustment of the automatic level
rule_summary_en: Officers MAY raise the automatic VPR or VPER level on indications not captured by the form; the text provides no downward modification.
source_locations: SES-4-2019 1.6 p.7 | SES-4-2019 5.10 p.14 | SES-4-2019 Preamble (describing the protocols then in force) p.2
correction_note: Pages confirmed (p. 7; p. 14). Added the preamble showing the rule pre-dates 2019.
accountability_trail: Override visible only as the final level; no reason-recording duty is stated.
interpretive_note: Instrucción 7/2016 rule 1.5 already had it (Module 2, thesis Annex 6).

decision_point: Which form after a new event
rule_summary_en: A significant event (new complaint, breach) triggers a VPER-C; otherwise VPER-S, which MAY also be done on new information or on request of the court or prosecutor.
correction_note: Added the request and new-information triggers.

rule_summary_en: Bajo, medio, alto and extremo: first VPER after the first judicial action resolving the protection request, at most SEVEN days after the VPR. No apreciado: only if judicial measures are obtained.
correction_note: v1 labelled this "routine medium or above"; the 2019 rule covers BAJO and above. v1 called 5.5 an "exceptional pathway" to the maximum: it is a minimum wait (see 2019-R23).

rule_summary_en: After the first VPER, without incidents, while active: extremo <72 h, alto <7 d, medio <30 d, bajo <60 d, no apreciado <90 d ("antes de").

decision_point: Sending a VPER result to court and prosecutor
rule_summary_en: VPER-S: individual oficio to court and prosecutor whenever the risk varies (up or down). VPER-C: the result goes into the new police file.
correction_note: Clarified that 5.11 covers VPER-S only.

decision_owner: police unit (floor set by SES designers)
rule_summary_en: Each level carries compulsory, immediate measures (Anexo 1), cumulative across levels and adapted to the case; officers may add others.
source_locations: SES-4-2019 3.1 p.10 | SES-4-2019 4.4 p.11 | SES-4-2019 Anexo 1 (header) p.15 | SES-4-2019 Anexo 1 (header) p.15
correction_note: Annex pages are 15-18 (v1: 15-19; p. 19 starts Anexo 2). Full annex now transcribed (26 items).
accountability_trail: No duty to record each measure taken is stated in the 2019 protocol.

rule_summary_en: If level measures exceed the evaluator's decision-making or operational capacity, inform those who allocate human and material resources and record the incident.

A unit MAY inactivate no-apreciado cases as a general rule and bajo cases exceptionally, if ALL hold: no judicial measures in force; the circumstances do not advise otherwise in the evaluator's judgement; for bajo, at least one contact and a 5.3 reassessment that did not raise the level.
correction_note: v1 omitted the evaluator-judgement premise and the "sin que este se haya elevado" condition.
interpretive_note: The judgement premise is negative: inactivation unless circumstances advise otherwise.

rule_summary_en: Two states: active (direct police control, level measures) and inactive (may be reactivated). Bajo and above are active as a general rule.
source_locations: SES-4-2019 2 (Inactivación de casos) p.9 | SES-4-2019 2.5 p.9

rule_summary_en: PSP provided at (after) the first VPER, whatever the level; officers deselect inapplicable measures or sections.
With an order of protection or other personal measure the case stays active, level measures are compulsory, and police ensure compliance with the order.
The VPR may be repeated until the file is sent to court; the last is the consolidated VPR. No time limit is stated.

decision_point: Initial report to court and prosecutor
rule_summary_en: The VPR result goes to court and prosecutor as an automated report (indicators marked Si/No, result), with exceptional diligencias for specially relevant cases and for minors in a vulnerable situation.

Any level MAY be inactivated when protection is impossible or unnecessary (victim not located for at least ONE month, death, departure abroad or custody of either party, analogous); causes recorded. Also on the victim's voluntary, manifest and repeated renunciation, at any level, if no judicial measures; a report goes to the prosecutor.
correction_note: v1 gave no thresholds; added the one-month rule, any-level renunciation and the prosecutor report.
accountability_trail: Causes recorded; prosecutor report on renunciation.

rule_summary_en: New complaint against the same aggressor: VPR if six months or more since the last assessment, otherwise VPER-C. Other causes (prison release, return to Spain): reactivation by VPER-S whatever the time inactive. General duty to reactivate when circumstances advise it.
source_locations: SES-4-2019 5.8 p.13 | SES-4-2019 5.9 p.13 | SES-4-2019 2 (closing paragraph) p.10

rule_summary_en: Medio, alto or extremo cases whose order was refused stay active with level measures; no-apreciado and bajo cases without measures may follow the inactivation rules.

other_actors: court; prosecutor; victim-support offices; social services
rule_summary_en: Where the victim renounces or, without renouncing, obstructs protection, police inform court and prosecutor in detail and promote contact by other institutions.
Exceptionally, for cases the system flags as specially relevant, the first VPER is done only after AT LEAST seven days (to await and obtain any forensic assessment). No maximum is stated.
correction_note: Split from v1 2019-R05, where it was read as an exception to the 7-day maximum.

rule_summary_en: Without a complaint, police act ex officio, including the risk assessment, and state the absence of a complaint to court and prosecutor.
correction_note: Shows the duty pre-dates Protocolo Cero (5/2021).

rule_summary_en: No direct questions to the victim during the assessment, save very specific cases where a datum can only be obtained that way.
interpretive_note: No equivalent clause in the 2025 protocol body (Annex I gives interview guidance instead).

rule_summary_en: An order of protection is communicated expressly to victim and aggressor, with its scope and the consequences of a breach.

decision_point: Initial VPR: who records the indicators
rule_summary_en: Instructing officers complete the VPR, never the victim, only with sufficient corroborated information; they must contrast sources and reduce "No se sabe" answers as far as possible.

decision_owner: system (DG Coordinación y Estudios; form designers)
rule_summary_en: Four levels: Bajo, Medio, Alto, Extremo. "No apreciado" disappears; Bajo is subdivided for risk management by whether judicial measures are in force.
source_locations: SES-1-2025 3.8 p.14 | SES-1-2025 1 (Cuestiones preliminares) p.11 | SES-1-2025 1 (Cuestiones preliminares) p.11
correction_note: Added p. 11 (removal of no apreciado; split of Bajo).

decision_point: Officer adjustment of the automatic level
rule_summary_en: The result MAY be raised by the officer at the end of each complete assessment, on indications not reflected in the form. The definitions speak of modifying the result and of the officer adopting the final decision "in agreement or disagreement", but the operative clauses provide only upward modification.
source_locations: SES-1-2025 3.8 p.14 | SES-1-2025 6.2 p.17 | SES-1-2025 1 (definitions) p.8 | SES-1-2025 1 (Cuestiones preliminares) p.10
correction_note: Added the definitional language, which is broader than the operative rule.

decision_point: Which form after a new event
rule_summary_en: VPR (not VPER) for a significant event: new complaint or breach of measures by the aggressor. VPER during follow-up without reoffending, and it MUST be done when new information arises; on a request from court or prosecutor, VPER unless the request concerns a possible reoffence (then VPR).
correction_note: Added the new-information and request triggers.

rule_summary_en: Medio, Alto, Extremo: first VPER after the first judicial action resolving the protection request, at most 15 days after the VPR. Bajo: the same only if judicial measures result. Bajo without measures: no first-VPER deadline is stated.
correction_note: v1 described the special-relevance clause as an exception to the deadline; it is a minimum wait (2025-R23).

rule_summary_en: After the first VPER, without known incidents, while active: Extremo <72 h, Alto <7 d, Medio <30 d, Bajo <60 d with judicial measures or penalties in force, <90 d without.
interpretive_note: The interval for supervised cases is not stated.

decision_point: Sending a VPER result to court and prosecutor
rule_summary_en: The VPER result is sent individually to court and prosecutor ONLY when the level rises.
accountability_trail: Oficio with the police reference; a decrease leaves no individual communication under this clause.

decision_owner: police unit (floor set by SES designers)
rule_summary_en: Each level carries compulsory, immediate measures (Annex II), cumulative, personalised and clearly communicated; officers may add others.
source_locations: SES-1-2025 5.1 p.15 | SES-1-2025 5.6 p.16 | SES-1-2025 5.6 p.16 | SES-1-2025 Anexo II (header) p.37 | SES-1-2025 Anexo II (header) p.37
correction_note: Full annex now transcribed (41 items).

rule_summary_en: If level measures exceed the evaluator's or managers' capacity, inform those who allocate resources; the incident must be recorded in VioGén-2.

Only Bajo cases MAY be inactivated, if: no criminal judicial measures (incl. "medidas condicionadas") in force; the circumstances reliably show, in the evaluator's judgement, that the objective conditions for a repeat are absent; at least one contact with the victim (preferably in person); a reassessment after the first judicial action that granted no protection. Actions must be traceable. Cases meeting a supervision criterion go to supervision first.
correction_note: Pages are 17-18 (v1: 17). v1 paraphrase "professional assessment supports it" missed that the 2025 premise is a positive finding ("de manera fehaciente").
accountability_trail: Traceability of contact and reassessment required.

rule_summary_en: Three states: active (general rule with judicial measures or Medio+), inactive, supervised (inactivation delayed for specific supervision actions).
source_locations: SES-1-2025 7 (Casos activos) p.17 | SES-1-2025 7 (Casos supervisados) p.17
correction_note: v1 note attributed the supervised state to "2022/2024"; it comes from Instrucción 2/2024 (11/2022 concerns resistant cases).

rule_summary_en: Before inactivation, a case is supervised if: special relevance / minors at risk at any point in the last year; Medio+ at any point in the last three months; or 2+ further complaints in the first six months. Procedure: VPER on entry; minimum 3 months, extendable once by 3 at the specialised officers' judgement (special relevance: up to two extensions, interview at first VPER, VPER and contact with the accused at 3 months). A new complaint makes the case active; exit requires a VPER at Bajo and an interview.
correction_note: v1 said "recent" special relevance; the text says "at any point in the last year". Added extension, exit and new-complaint rules.

rule_summary_en: PSP agreed with the victim at the first VPER or earlier; officers deselect inapplicable measures; the victim is told her level "por un medio que deje constancia en derecho".
correction_note: Added 5.4.

rule_summary_en: Court orders are communicated to victim and aggressor; judicial measures keep the case active as a general rule and set the Bajo interval (60 vs 90 days).
The VPR may be repeated until the file goes to court; the last one is the consolidated VPR, within a maximum of 72 hours.

decision_point: Initial report to court and prosecutor
rule_summary_en: Automated report always includes indicators marked Si/No/NS and the result; additional diligencias for special relevance, minors at risk and persistent aggressors.
correction_note: Added that "No se sabe" (NS) answers are now visible to the court.

rule_summary_en: Assessment and measures proceed whether or not a complaint was made, acting under Protocolo Cero; the absence of a complaint is stated to court and prosecutor.
correction_note: v1 said a 2019/2025 comparison "cannot establish introduction" because of Protocolo Cero; in fact the ex officio duty is already in the 2019 text (C19-PREC); Protocolo Cero (2021) added first-contact procedure.

rule_summary_en: For aggressors with prior records against other women the system generates an additional diligencia for court and prosecutor, which the acting officers must complete with case specifics.

Inactivation "se procederá" at any level when protection is impossible or unnecessary: victim not located for at least THREE months since last contact (then judicial police continue the search and an oficio informs court and prosecutor), death, departure abroad (unless the protecting officer decides otherwise), custody, analogous circumstances. Causes and actions recorded and communicated to court and prosecutor.
correction_note: v1 gave no specifics; added thresholds and duties. Note the modal shift from "podrá" (2019) to "se procederá".
accountability_trail: Causes, actions, communication to court and prosecutor.

rule_summary_en: On the victim's voluntary, manifest and repeated renunciation, inactivation only at Bajo or Medio and only without judicial measures; officers must look into the reasons and an oficio informs court and prosecutor.

decision_point: Reactivation after a new complaint or breach
rule_summary_en: An inactive case with a new complaint against the same aggressor, or a verified breach, is reactivated with a new VPR; court and prosecutor are informed.

After an exceptional inactivation, reactivation requires a VPER result of Medio or higher, unless judicial measures are still in force. For releases from prison in (past) special-relevance VG cases: VPR plus a personal interview.
accountability_trail: Recorded as an exception to the form rules.

rule_summary_en: Special-relevance cases at Medio or Alto: first VPER only after at least 7 days (to avoid a sharp drop in risk and await forensic assessment). Extremo may be reassessed earlier at the specialised officers' judgement once dangers are controlled.
correction_note: Replaces v1's reading of 4.5 as an exception to the 15-day maximum.

rule_summary_en: The system detects special relevance and minors at risk from indicator combinations and sends automated diligencias recommending further (forensic) assessment.
interpretive_note: The combinations themselves are not public.

rule_summary_en: If a case was once special relevance / minors at risk but the latest assessment does not flag it, the system displays the history.

decision_point: Telling the victim about the aggressor's record
rule_summary_en: Only when Medio-with-special-relevance, Alto or Extremo, four named indicators, grave violence and prior complaints by other victims in the last five years coincide, and the officer judges it proportionate and necessary: the victim is told only that "los datos de la persona denunciada constan en el Sistema VioGén-2". Never systematic; recorded.

Extra measures for persistent aggressors (tell him control may extend to other victims, stricter order supervision, prison movements, record in device requests); if also special relevance: VPER of his other active victims and contact with victims inactivated less than 90 days ago.
Where the victim obstructs or renounces protection: inform court and prosecutor expressly, promote contact by OAVD and social services, and issue an oficio announcing inactivation under 7.2.
After a VG homicide the case is not inactivated; the Central Administration records the information.

The system has no machine learning and its cut-offs do not change with operation; the final assessment is adopted by the officer. The DG Coordinación y Estudios is responsible for the system's processing and functioning.
source_locations: SES-1-2025 1 (Cuestiones preliminares) p.10 | SES-1-2025 1 (Cuestiones preliminares) p.10 | SES-1-2025 Instrucción SEGUNDA p.3 | SES-1-2025 1 (definitions) p.8
interpretive_note: A statement about the design, not its parameters; the weights and cut-offs are not published.

rule_summary_en: Recording the protection measures actually applied (Módulo de Actuaciones Policiales) is "recomendable", "en la medida de lo posible". By contrast, capacity shortfalls, inactivation causes and supervision interviews must be recorded.
accountability_trail: Weak duty: the delivery of measures may leave no record.

rule_summary_en: A possible breach reported by Cometa is checked; once verified, diligencias are instructed with the Cometa report and a VPR follows.
